Meta has invested $182.9 billion in AI infrastructure. With limited direct revenue from its own AI models, it is now looking to rent out its data center capacity to other companies.

The Bright Side:
This move prevents the massive data centers from becoming stranded assets, potentially lowering costs for smaller AI developers.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a WHAT error; the company is shifting from a product-led strategy to an infrastructure-led strategy to survive the high costs of AI development.

Social Physics Analysis:
By opening its infrastructure to the market, Meta is moving from a closed, proprietary model to a more collaborative, utility-based approach, reducing the strain of its massive capital expenditure.

The Trajectory: The Path of Awakening.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Grace. The shift reflects a pragmatic adjustment to market realities.

The Unavoidable Truth: Meta needs revenue to justify its massive AI spending.

The Unavoidable Lie: Meta's AI models are currently driving significant standalone revenue.
